instruction: Locate the document attached to the newest email in the Notes folder and move it to the Downloads folder, naming it 'notes.docx'.

metadata.explanation: Task requires saving the attached docx file from the email in Notes folder to the Downloads directory with a specific filename 'notes.docx' (different from original 'lecture-notes.docx'). The evaluator checks if the file exists at /home/user/Downloads/notes.docx with a minimum size of 1000 bytes. This tests the ability to both save an attachment and rename it during the save process. Custom getter retrieves file info from VM, and custom metric verifies file existence and size.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies file saved to correct directory (/home/user/Downloads/)
Evaluator correctly verifies renamed filename ('notes.docx' instead of original name)
Evaluator correctly verifies file has content via size check (>= 1000 bytes)
Getter logic is sound: uses env.controller.get_file() to check file existence and retrieve size
Metric logic is correct: checks exists=True and size >= min_size
Type mismatch warning (Dict vs Optional[Dict]) is benign - getter always returns dict, never None
Limitation: Does not verify file source (that it came from most recent email in Notes folder) - relies on end-to-end assumption in controlled environment
Limitation: Does not verify file is actually a .docx document beyond size check (no magic bytes or content validation)
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding file type validation by checking magic bytes (docx files should start with 'PK' as they are ZIP archives)
Consider adding a checksum or content hash comparison if the expected attachment content is known
The static validator type warning can be ignored - the getter always returns a dict, so runtime behavior is correct
